affected_boundaries: durable scheduler action to host-managed worktree lifecycle

observed_behavior: RECOVER_WORKTREE could not start when the missing checkout had no archived artifact identity in the worker chat.
expected_behavior: The same worker session reconstructs its original checkout from its recorded main worktree even when its cwd and attached archive identity are absent.
causal_mechanism: The host-action contract equated every missing managed checkout with an archived artifact and required restoration at the extinct path, but Codex restore accepts only artifact identities actually attached to the chat.

anti_pattern.structural_description: A resumable action prescribed one reconstruction mechanism without recording or proving that the required ephemeral artifact identity existed.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: Durable Git and scheduler state can survive physical checkout loss while the optional host archive identity does not, leaving the prescribed action impossible despite sufficient state to reconstruct the checkout safely.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Recovery preserves worker identity and authenticated Git state without requiring the missing checkout or an optional host artifact as a precondition.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: The previous create-worktree correction had Git fixture proof, not proof that the host could create from a missing cwd. Worker-owned recovery now resolves a durable attachment capability before repository preflight and reconstructs the exact original path from recorded main-worktree provenance; live host continuity remains a separate gate.

applicability_conditions: A durable workflow retains a live session and recoverable Git revision after its physical managed checkout disappears.
The host distinguishes archived-artifact restoration from new managed-checkout creation.
known_non_matches: A missing checkout with no authenticated session, binding, branch, or preserved revision remains unrecoverable.
A delivered revision can continue through integration without reconstructing its checkout.
confirmation_evidence: The worker reported an empty artifact inventory and restore_worktree rejected recovery because no archive identity existed.
The previous focused regression re-provisioned a different Git path but did not prove the Codex creation API could run from an absent worker cwd.
The stakeholder's subsequent worker report said the supported create-worktree call failed with Not a git repository.
A real CLI regression failed at the authentication hook's repository lookup; after correction the same command reconstructed the original path from a neutral cwd without a coordinator action.
regression_proofs: tests/worker-worktrees.test.js: original worker recovers its exact checkout from a neutral cwd without coordinator action
tests/worker-worktrees.test.js: recovery rebuilds a removed slot directory with or without a surviving Git registration
tests/worker-worktrees.test.js: worker-owned recovery acknowledges the original pending action without a new coordinator observation
